§3.2.3: 'p- and k-, which became respectively v- and y- in Kone have been easily re-introduced in initial position'; all words with p- but one come from Pwaamei or Pwapwâ (pad 'to warm up', pom 'butterfly', piu 'star' re-introduced in Haveke).
§3.2.3: k- borrowed back in Kone, from Polynesian, the northern and the southern mainland (kathia 'leprosy', kele 'the strangles', kuha 'gun').
